Sasha: Heads-up — I’m seeing a p99 latency spike on the reranker/embeds non-chat endpoint after the kernel-selection tweak we rolled at 03:00 UTC. Profiler attached in thread (summary below).

Omar: which kernel? the optimized-attn path or the fallback fast-gemm?

Sasha: optimized-attn for 8-bit quant models (q4f16) — selector picked it more aggressively for short sequences. p50 is fine, but p99 jumped from ~85ms to ~210ms on small-reqs load.

Devon: that smells like KV cache behavior — small sequences + aggressive kernel sometimes causes extra memcpy / cache invalidation. Did the profiler show KV miss spikes?

Sasha: yes — KV miss rate up ~3x for these requests. Also saw more short-lived allocations in the serving runtime. Flame snippet:

```
CPU: memcpy 32%
GPU kernel launch latency up 2ms avg
KV cache lock contention (spin) 12%
Batch formation latency increased by ~1.6x for priority windowed queues
```

Maria: what was the batch-formation policy during the run? window size, early-fill, token-budget?

Sasha: running canary config: window_ms=10, early_fill_pct=40, token_budget_target=1500, prefill_slots=2. But because many requests were 8-16 tokens, token_budget heuristics created many tiny batches that ended up invoking the optimized-attn kernel with an unfavorable memory layout.

Kyler: interesting — so tiny batches + kernel choice triggers memcpy thrash. Two levers: bias kernel selector to choose fast-gemm for <32 tokens OR adjust batch formation to combine more small requests before firing.

Omar: prefer changing batch heuristics first — easier to A/B. Try increasing window_ms to 18 and increase early_fill_pct to 60 for non-chat rerankers in the next canary. That should allow coalescing tiny requests to fewer GPU kernels.

Devon: agreed but watch latency SLO for tail — coalescing helps throughput but can add ~5–10ms to p50. We should set per-route token_budget_target override: for rerank/nonchat set target=3000 and min_batch_size=4.

Maria: quick config snippet we can push to canary:

```
routes:
  /v1/embeds/rerank-nonchat:
    batching:
      window_ms: 18
      early_fill_pct: 60
      token_budget_target: 3000
      min_batch_size: 4
      prefill_slots: 1
    kernel_selector:
      prefer_kernel_for_short_seq: false
      override_threshold_tokens: 32
```

Sasha: pushed that config to staging — running load job with realistic seq distribution (60% 8–20 tok, 30% 30–60 tok, 10% >100). Initial observation: batch sizes up from median 2 -> median 6; p99 dropped back toward baseline (now ~95ms). KV miss rate normalized.

perf-bot: perf/regression-checker completed for staging canary (run id perf-20260311-09). Results summary: p50 delta +7ms, p95 delta +12ms, p99 delta -110ms vs previous canary. Memory alloc churn reduced by 45%.

Omar: that’s promising. A few follow-ups: 1) make kernel selector respect per-route overrides so we don’t accidentally pick optimized-attn for small seqs on rerankers; 2) add a queue-shaping metric that penalizes sequences <16 tokens unless batch_size>=3.

Kyler: FYI I dug into kernel selection logs — the selector uses seq_len_p50 heuristic but we accidentally fed it per-host aggregated stats, which biased it after the change. Fix is to use per-route distribution and a decay window of 5m. I’ll send a patch.

Devon: also want a microbench: run microbench for optimized-attn vs fast-gemm with batch_size 4 and seq_len 12/20/40 and KV cache warm vs cold. Need numbers before the rollout.

Sasha: running microbench now, attaching table soon.

Sasha: microbench quick results (batch_size 4):
- seq12 warm-KV: fast-gemm p99=88ms, opt-attn p99=240ms
- seq12 cold-KV: fast-gemm p99=120ms, opt-attn p99=310ms
- seq40 warm-KV: opt-attn p99=130ms, fast-gemm p99=180ms

Maria: that confirms kernel crossover point around ~28–32 tokens. Kernel selector override_threshold_tokens: 32 is a good default.

Omar: rollout plan: 1% prod traffic with new batching config + per-route kernel override, monitor p99, KV miss rate, and batch-size histogram. If stable after 2h, ramp to 10% then 50%. Canary job id: canary-emb-rerank-0311.

Kyler: I pushed selector patch to PR #1289 — it adds per-route histograms and decay window. Also added a metric export kernel_select_reason.

perf-bot: alert created: perf-alert/emb-rerank if p99 > 160ms for 5m at 1% traffic.

Devon: note — we should persist a short term cache of recent small-batch signatures to avoid repeated KV evictions for the same client bursty patterns. Idea: soft-kv-reserve per-client for 2s. Thoughts?

Sasha: I like soft-kv-reserve. Low-risk: implement as heuristic in runtime that pins recent KV slots for short TTL (2s) when batch_size < 4 observed. Add metric kv_reserve_hit.

Maria: OK — let’s run the 1% canary with both batching tweak and kernel override only first. If that looks good after 4h, enable soft-kv-reserve in a second canary. Keeps variables small.

Omar: agreed. Action items:
- Kyler: merge selector patch and deploy to canary (ETA 2h)
- Sasha: watch canary metrics + run microbench (in progress)
- Devon: prepare perf-blocking test with KV warm/cold patterns
- Maria: create canary run + dashboard with batch-size histogram, kernel_select_reason, kv_miss_rate, p50/p95/p99

Sasha: noted. Will post results in this thread — initial staging run looks good. Thanks all :thumbsup:

perf-bot: deploy: canary/emb-rerank-0311 started at 2026-03-11T09:42:51Z

Sasha: (follow-up) staging microbench full CSV attached to artifact store: s3://redwood-perf/emb-rerank/microbench/20260311.csv

Kyler: merged PR and started canary deploy. Monitoring now.

Omar: thanks — if p99 stays <160ms at 1% for 30m we can bump to 10% and collect longer-run KV/churn stats.

Sasha: will update in ~45m with first window metrics.
